exact_poly.note: polynomial for the unit right triangle, A twice its root; Galois group S₇ (Sudermann-Merx), so no radical form exists

proof.title: E. Hendren, A computer-assisted proof of optimality for Heilbronn's problem with eight points in a triangle, Zenodo (November 2026)

coordinates_source.note: exact realization of the certified optimum: each coordinate an explicit degree-7 algebraic number, identified here from the tie system (minimal polynomials in data/sources/exact/triangle-n08-coordinate-minpolys.json)

changelog.text: exact realization of the certified optimum: tie system solved to 400 digits, every coordinate identified as an explicit degree-7 algebraic number (this site); replaces the reconstruction

status changed from proven to numerically optimal: the certificate (arXiv:2607.15021) is a Gurobi run with a 10⁻⁴ relative MIP gap in floating point, and the exact optimum (the septic root) remains a conjecture of Chen, Zeng and Zhou

computer-assisted proof of optimality posted by Ethan Hendren: an exact-arithmetic branch and bound over the whole configuration space (LP bounds verified in exact integer arithmetic, neighbourhood of the optimum closed by an interval-arithmetic certificate) shows that the value is twice the unique real root of the septic, with the known configuration unique up to symmetry; AI-assisted and not yet independently verified, so the entry stays numerically optimal

optimality proof with a replayable certificate trace (Ethan Hendren): a second, independent proof by the cell-graph method records every split and closure, 2,950 shards and 4,379,630 closures, replayed in exact arithmetic by a separate checker that does not use the search code (it also re-checks the local certificate: Newton-Kantorovich existence and the first-order basin); trace, checker and release receipt archived on Zenodo; AI-assisted, and so far replayed only by its author
